Subject: Brightlane sizing — internal draft notes

Team,

I pulled the workbook and sketched two feasible topologies. High-level conclusions:

1) Carveout (per-tenant dedicated slab) — lowest isolation risk, predictable headroom
   - Rough sizing: 6 x A800 (or equivalent) per tenant lane to meet 18k toks/s if traffic is mostly short-chat.
   - NIC: recommend 200Gbps per host aggregation / 400Gbps at leaf for egress headroom to avoid head-of-line under burst.
   - Pros: strict isolation, simpler billing split.
   - Cons: higher idle cost, harder to absorb 3x burst unless we pre-warm.

2) Multiplex slab (shared GPU pool with admission & soft reservations) — cost-efficient
   - Rough sizing: 24 x A800 across pool with admission control, prefix KV cache warmup, and 2-level QoS.
   - Admission policy: reserve 30% of capacity for critical tenants; soft slots for others.
   - Pros: better amortization of burst, easier to meet 3x short bursts via admission thinning.

Network/peering notes:
- Egress to other clouds: Brightlane's north-south at us-west-2 has a NAT GW setup in AZ-a; we should recommend cross-AZ egress peering to avoid bottlenecks on NAT.
- Inter-AZ latency: <0.5ms expected; we still recommend colocating cache/coordinator services in same AZ cluster for lowest tail.

Action items (for first-pass proposal):
- Jonas: produce per-GPU token/sec profile for short vs long requests (including KV cache hit / miss multipliers).
- Karthik: run network saturation calc (ingress+egress) for both topologies and recommend NIC sizing and peering.
- Dylan/Marissa: prepare ops playbook stub (warm pools, pre-warm job cadence, eviction policy).

I'll merge into a short proposal and share with Brightlane by Tue EOD.

- Laura

Subject: Re: Brightlane sizing — per-GPU throughput profiles attached

Laura / Dylan — attaching a quick CSV and the generated per-GPU profiles. Highlights:
- Short-chat (<=64 tokens): one warmed A800 can do ~1,100–1,300 toks/sec (KV cache hit), tail spikes to 1,600 on bursts for small payloads.
- Long batches (>512 tokens): amortized throughput drops — expect ~150 toks/sec per GPU (memory and seq-length bound).
- Cache warmup: cold KV miss reduces short-chat per-GPU throughput by ~35% for first ~5k requests.

Implication: if Brightlane's traffic is >70% short-chat, the multiplex plan with 24 GPUs should comfortably cover 18k sustained with admission and warm cache. If long-batch fraction is higher, carveouts with more GPUs per tenant are safer.

Attachments: brightlane_gpu_profiles.csv

— Jonas
